data.text:
Claim 0: Golden Gate anchorages weigh about 60,000 tons each. Supported as written.
- The Golden Gate Bridge Highway and Transportation District statistics page lists the total weight of each anchorage as 60,000 tons (54,400,000 kg). Source: https://www.goldengate.org/bridge/history-research/statistics-data/design-construction-stats/
- A 1935 US Naval Institute Proceedings article (pre-construction) estimated about 120,000 tons each; the as-built official figure of 60,000 tons is the reliable one. Source: https://www.usni.org/magazines/proceedings/1935/april/golden-gate-and-san-francisco-bay-bridges

Claim 1: Tacoma Narrows twisted and collapsed in 1940 in a wind of only about 40 mph (64 km/h). Supported as written.
- History.com: the bridge collapsed on November 7, 1940 in winds of about 40 mph through aeroelastic flutter. Source: https://www.history.com/this-day-in-history/tacoma-narrows-bridge-collapses
- University of Western Ontario page: winds about 42 mph; gusts 38 mph in the early morning and 42 mph two hours later. Source: https://www.eng.uwo.ca/people/esavory/tacoma_narrows_bridge_collapse.htm
- Live Science: collapse on Nov 7, 1940 forced a rethink of structural engineering. Source: https://www.livescience.com/technology/engineering/science-history-the-tacoma-narrows-bridge-collapses-forcing-a-complete-rethink-in-structural-engineering-nov-7-1940
- Sources give 40 to 42 mph; "about 40 mph" is fair.

Claim 2: Each Golden Gate main cable is made of 27,572 steel wires. Supported as written.
- Golden Gate Bridge District, Main Cable Statistics: 27,572 galvanized steel wires per main cable, in 61 strands. Source: https://goldengate.org/exhibits/cross-section-of-a-main-cable
- The Engineer (August 1936): strands range from 256 to 472 wires, so 452 per strand is an average; the total 27,572 stands. Source: https://theengineer.co.uk/august-1936-the-cables-of-the-golden-gate-bridge
